published.citation: Esteves et al. 2015, dayside brightness temperature in the Kepler band, assuming no reflected light: 2400 +/- 100 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...804..150E/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse in the Kepler band (Kepler) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the paper's value from an eclipse 44 ppm deep (+15, -16); no infrared eclipse is published
